title: Lifting a prescribed finite-free derived model modulo a Jacobson ideal
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative unital ring and $I\subset R$ an ideal such that every element of $1+I$ is invertible. Let $K\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Write $Q_R$ and $Q_{R/I}$ for the localization functors from complexes to the respective derived categories, and write $L=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$ for derived extension of scalars [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the one-object point site. Let $F^\bullet$ be a complex of finite free $R/I$-modules, let $b\in\mathbb Z$, and assume $F^i=0$ for $i>b$. For every specified isomorphism $\alpha:L(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{R/I}(F^\bullet)$, there exist a complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules with $P^i=0$ for $i>b$, an isomorphism $\beta:Q_R(P^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, and an isomorphism of complexes $\theta:P^\bullet\otimes_R R/I\xrightarrow{\sim}F^\bullet$ such that
$$Q_{R/I}(\theta)\circ c_P=\alpha\circ L(\beta),$$
where $c_P:L(Q_R(P^\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{R/I}(P^\bullet\otimes_R R/I)$ is the canonical comparison computed on the bounded-above free, hence K-flat, complex $P^\bullet$. No nilpotence of $I$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BCB, lemma-lift-complex-stably-frees, finite-free case; Tag 0BCA, lemma-lift-complex, proof with delta chosen to represent the inverse of the specified alpha; preservation of the cutoff follows by finite Nakayama (Tag 00DV).

proof.text: Put $S=R/I$, and write $\overline M=S\otimes_R M$ for modules and termwise for complexes. Use the class $\mathcal P$ of finite projective $R$-modules in the lifting lemmas. This class satisfies their sum/summand condition: projectivity of a direct sum follows by lifting its two component maps along a surjection; projectivity of a summand follows by extending a map by zero on its complement and restricting a lift. For finiteness, concatenate generating sets for a sum and project a finite generating set onto a summand. These are the lifting characterization of projectivity and direct-sum operations, with no freeness claim about arbitrary projective summands. Maps between class members that are surjective after reduction are surjective by the cited finite Nakayama consequence. The zero module belongs to the class.

Pseudo-coherence supplies a bounded-above finite-free complex $H$ and $h:Q_RH\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Free modules are projective and projective modules are flat, so $H$ is K-flat by the bounded-above flat criterion. Its canonical computation isomorphism is $c_H:L(Q_RH)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S\overline H$. The bounded-above projective complex $F$ represents every derived map out of $Q_SF$ by a chain map. Choose $\delta:F\to\overline H$ whose derived class is exactly
$$Q_S\delta=c_H\circ L(h^{-1})\circ\alpha^{-1}.$$
This is an isomorphism, so $\delta$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This choice retains the specified marking rather than merely choosing some isomorphism between the two derived objects.

source.place: Tag 0BCA (lemma-lift-complex), first paragraph, choosing delta; Tag 064B (derived-lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex); Tag 064K (more-algebra-lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism)

proof.text: Form the actual cone $C=\operatorname{Cone}(\delta)$, with $C^i=\overline H^i\oplus F^{i+1}$ and differential $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Hx+\delta y,-d_Fy)$. The cone-properties node makes it bounded above and acyclic. Each term is a finite-free $S$-module, hence is the reduction of a finite-free $R$-module, which belongs to $\mathcal P$. Apply the acyclic-complex lifting node to this $C$ and the class verified in step 1. It gives a bounded-above acyclic $R$-complex $A$ with finite projective terms and an isomorphism $e:\overline A\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. No nilpotence or completeness is used in this application.

The strict-map node lifts the cone inclusion $j:\overline H\to C$ to $f:H\to A$ with $e\circ\overline f=j$. Let $B=\operatorname{coker}(f)$ as an actual complex, with quotient $g:A\to B$. The cone-cokernel node identifies $\overline B$ with $F[1]$ and says that the reduced cokernel sequence is split in every degree. Choose its canonical identification $\eta:\overline B\xrightarrow{\sim}F[1]$: in degree $i$ the quotient class of $a$ maps to the second coordinate of $e^i(\overline a)$. It is well-defined and bijective because the reduced quotient is the cokernel of $x\mapsto(x,0)$, and it commutes with differentials because the second cone differential is $-d_F$. Thus $\eta\circ\overline g=\operatorname{pr}_F\circ e$. For each $i$, apply the reduced-splitting node to $H^i\to A^i\to B^i$. Its first two terms lie in $\mathcal P$, and $\overline B^i\cong F^{i+1}$ is the reduction of a finite free module. Hence the original sequence is short exact and $B^i\in\mathcal P$. It is split in each degree by projectivity of $B^i$. Boundedness above follows from $B^i$ being a quotient of $A^i$.

source.place: Tag 0BCA (lemma-lift-complex), dotted arrow, cokernel, and final split-injectivity paragraphs

proof.text: Set $P=B[-1]$ and let $\theta:\overline P\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ be $\eta[-1]$, with the canonical cancellation of the shifts. The terms of $P$ are finite projective. Because $\overline P^i\cong F^i$ is free, the finite-projective/free-reduction node makes every $P^i$ free. For $i>b$ its reduction is zero. Apply the finite Nakayama surjectivity node to $0\to P^i$: its reduction is surjective, so the original map is surjective and $P^i=0$. This preserves the specified cutoff even though the acyclic lift may initially have had a larger bound. The complexes $H,A,B,P$ have projective, hence flat, terms and are bounded above, so all four are K-flat by the cited criterion.

The sequence $0\to H\xrightarrow f A\xrightarrow g B\to0$ has its canonical derived triangle and boundary $s:Q_RB\to Q_RH[1]$. Acyclicity identifies $Q_RA$ with zero: the map $0\to A$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Exactness of Hom into this triangle and its rotations makes $s$ an isomorphism: for every $W$, $\operatorname{Hom}(W,s)$ is surjective and has zero kernel because the adjacent Hom groups into $Q_RA$ and $Q_RA[1]$ vanish. Taking $W=Q_RH[1]$ gives a right inverse and injectivity for $W=Q_RB$ makes it a left inverse. Write $t:Q_RP\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_RH$ for $s[-1]$ under the canonical shifts and put $\beta=h\circ t$.

Compute the boundary of the reduced sequence using $e$ and $\eta$. It is the boundary of
$$0\to\overline H\xrightarrow{x\mapsto(x,0)}\operatorname{Cone}(\delta)\xrightarrow{(x,y)\mapsto y}F[1]\to0.$$
For its displayed splittings $\pi(x,y)=x$ and $u(y)=(0,y)$, the degree-$i$ boundary is $\pi^{i+1}d_C^iu^i(y)=\delta^{i+1}(y)$. The degreewise-split derived-triangle node therefore identifies this canonical boundary with $Q_S(\delta[1])$. In particular this calculation fixes the sign using the cone convention with third arrow minus the projection; no unspecified triangle isomorphism is chosen. Apply the ringed K-flat pullback/SES node on the point site to $R\to S$ and the sequence of step 6. Its flat-term and K-flat hypotheses were checked in step 5. Its boundary and shift identities, shifted by $-1$, give
$$c_H\circ L(t)=Q_S(\delta)\circ Q_S(\theta)\circ c_P.$$
Here $\theta$ is precisely the shifted quotient map fixed in step 5, so the comparison uses the same marking and not a replacement of it.

proof.text:
By the choice in step 2, $Q_S(\delta)\circ\alpha\circ L(h)=c_H$. Substitute the equation of step 7 and $\beta=h\circ t$ to obtain
$$\alpha\circ L(\beta)=\alpha\circ L(h)\circ c_H^{-1}\circ Q_S(\delta)\circ Q_S(\theta)\circ c_P=Q_S(\theta)\circ c_P.$$
Together with the finite freeness and exact cutoff of step 5, these are all the required data and the required equation.
